sources.note: An Italian proverb benchmark on which models complete proverbs successfully but fail multiple-choice selection when no correct option is present, with CoT analysis showing they name the right ending while failing to notice its absence.
sources.title: Easy to Complete, Hard to Choose: Investigating LLM Performance on the ProverbIT Benchmark

sources.note: Shows that the standard metric for judging contamination-mitigation strategies can be scored by cancellation rather than by restoration, replaces it with a per-question stratified metric under which the published ranking reverses, and proposes a mitigation that decides its intervention during decoding instead of from a prior estimate.
sources.title: Zero Gap Is Not Restoration: Stratified Per-Question Probability Evaluation and Step-wise Mitigation of Benchmark Contamination

sources.note: Reframes unlearning in reasoning models as an intervention on the CoT itself, having the model generate logically valid counterfactual traces and iteratively preference-tuning toward them.
sources.title: CiPO: Counterfactual Unlearning for Large Reasoning Models through Iterative Preference Optimization

sources.note: Reverse-engineers the arithmetic circuit down to individual neurons and finds it is neither a learned algorithm nor memorization, but an unordered collection of sparse heuristic neurons that each fire on a numerical input pattern and vote for corresponding answers.
sources.title: Arithmetic Without Algorithms: Language Models Solve Math With a Bag of Heuristics

sources.note: Shows that benchmark contamination in reasoning models is alarmingly easy to hide: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals contamination detectors rely on, and PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the cause — implying a broad class of RL methods conceals contamination inherently.
sources.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models

sources.note: Shows that transformers can learn implicit multi-step reasoning over stored knowledge, but only through grokking — extended training far past overfitting — and that whether the resulting circuit generalizes out of distribution depends on the reasoning type, succeeding for comparison and failing for composition.
sources.title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization

sources.note: Converts AMC23 and AIME24/25 into symbolic templates whose constants are replaced by sampled variables, requires a model to solve several instantiations of each problem, and finds RL-finetuned models lose most of their reported accuracy under that consistency requirement.
sources.title: VAR-MATH: Probing True Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs via Symbolic Multi-Instance Benchmarks

result.definition: Reproducing training content rather than computing an answer, and across 7 sources a hypothesis the archive tests rather than assumes. Its cleanest separation is the loose-versus-strict metric under symbolic variabilisation: a base mathematics model loses 38.5 percent even under partial credit, consistent with heavy reliance on memorised patterns, while reinforcement-trained models lose 2.6 to 7.2 -- so the two metrics together separate memorisation from mere inconsistency. A mechanistic source rules it out for arithmetic specifically, finding neither a learned algorithm nor memorisation but an unordered collection of sparse heuristic neurons voting. And a benchmark source finds the opposite asymmetry for proverbs, where completion is easy and choice is hard. The archive's related material covers the unlearning side and the contamination-detection side, where the standing result is that post-training suppresses the signals memorisation detectors rely on.
